intro: Amsterdam rewards visitors who wander its canals, museums and brown cafés at an easy pace. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Trams are the main way around; metro and buses fill the gaps, run by GVB.
Most routes run about 06:00 to midnight, with a few night buses.
Pay by tapping a contactless bank card (OVpay) or an OV-chipkaart.
Uber and Bolt work in Amsterdam; taxis are metered and pricey.
The centre is flat and compact, so walking and bikes are often fastest.
Free ferries cross the IJ behind Centraal station.

annefrank.name: Anne Frank House
annefrank.price_text: ≈ €16 adults · children 0–9 free · check current price
annefrank.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–22:00 in summer · shorter in winter · check on the day
annefrank.tip: Tickets sell out online weeks ahead and are timed. Book the first morning slot to avoid crowds.

vangogh.name: Van Gogh Museum
vangogh.price_text: ≈ €24 adults · under 18 free · check current price
vangogh.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–18:00 · later on some Fridays · check on the day
vangogh.tip: Only timed online tickets are sold. Go at opening or after 15:00 for quieter rooms.

rijksmuseum.name: Rijksmuseum
rijksmuseum.price_text: ≈ €25 adults · under 18 free · check current price
rijksmuseum.tip: Head straight to the Gallery of Honour for the Night Watch, then work backwards.

canalring.name: Canal Ring
canalring.tip: Walk the Herengracht and Keizersgracht at dusk when bridges light up. Watch for bikes on the narrow paths.

damsquare.name: Dam Square
damsquare.tip: A quick stop between sights. Use it as a meeting point, not a destination.

redlight.name: Red Light District
redlight.tip: No photos of windows. Walk in a small group and stay on the main lanes.

almondblossom.name: Almond Blossom
almondblossom.price_text: Included with Van Gogh Museum ticket
almondblossom.tip: This Van Gogh painting hangs in the museum. Ask staff which floor it is on that week.

amstel.name: Amstel River
amstel.tip: Walk the east bank near the Magere Brug for the classic river view.

canalcruise.name: Amsterdam Canal Cruise
canalcruise.tip: Choose a small open boat over a big glass-topped one. Book a sunset slot.

dungeon.name: Amsterdam Dungeon
dungeon.price_text: ≈ €27 adults · cheaper online · check current price
dungeon.tip: Actors jump out and it is dark. Skip it with small children or anyone who dislikes scares.

artis.name: Artis Royal Zoo
artis.price_text: ≈ €28 adults · children cheaper · check current price
artis.tip: Buy tickets online to skip the queue. The aquarium and planetarium are included.

dehaar.name: Castle De Haar
dehaar.price_text: ≈ €20 adults · park only cheaper · check current price
dehaar.hours: Roughly Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00 · closed some winter weeks · check on the day
dehaar.tip: It is outside the city, about an hour by train and bus. Book a castle entry slot online.

heineken.name: Heineken Experience
heineken.price_text: ≈ €25 adults · includes two drinks · check current price
heineken.tip: Book online for a time slot. Go before 13:00 to avoid the biggest groups.

cruijff.name: Johan Cruijff Arena
cruijff.price_text: ≈ €20 stadium tour · match tickets vary · check current price
cruijff.hours: Tour times vary by match schedule · check on the day
cruijff.tip: Check the fixture list first. On match days tours stop and trains get very busy.

keukenhof.name: Keukenhof
keukenhof.price_text: ≈ €20 entry · transport extra · check current price
keukenhof.hours: Open roughly mid-March to mid-May only · daily 08:00–19:00
keukenhof.tip: It is a seasonal garden, not year-round. Go on a weekday morning in April.

muiderslot.name: Muiderslot
muiderslot.hours: Roughly daily 10:00–17:00 · shorter in winter · check on the day
muiderslot.tip: A real moated castle about 45 minutes away by bus. Combine it with a walk in Muiden.

nemo.name: NEMO Science Museum
nemo.tip: The rooftop terrace is free and has a good city view. Great for kids on a rainy day.

oudvalkeveen.name: Oud Valkeveen
oudvalkeveen.hours: Seasonal, roughly April–October · check on the day
oudvalkeveen.tip: A small family play park outside the city. Only worth it if you travel with young children.

oudekerk.name: Oude Kerk
oudekerk.hours: Roughly daily 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
oudekerk.tip: Amsterdam's oldest building, now an art space. Check what exhibition is on before you go.

rijkslib.name: Rijksmuseum Library
rijkslib.tip: The Cuypers Library is inside the museum. It is a quiet photo stop most visitors miss.

concertgebouw.name: Royal Concertgebouw
concertgebouw.price_text: ≈ €25 and up · free lunch concerts exist · check programme
concertgebouw.hours: Box office and concerts vary · check on the day
concertgebouw.tip: The free Wednesday lunchtime concerts are a cheap way in. Arrive early, seats go fast.

royalpalace.name: Royal Palace Amsterdam
royalpalace.price_text: ≈ €13 adults · under 18 free · check current price
royalpalace.hours: Roughly daily 10:00–17:00 · closed during royal events · check on the day
royalpalace.tip: It closes when the royal family uses it. Check the calendar before you plan around it.

albertcuyp.name: Albert Cuyp Market
albertcuyp.tip: Try a fresh stroopwafel made in front of you. Bring cash for small stalls.

adamlookout.name: A'DAM Lookout
adamlookout.price_text: ≈ €16 observation deck · swing extra · check current price
adamlookout.tip: Take the free ferry from behind Central Station. Go near sunset for the best light.

jordaanwalk.name: Jordaan neighbourhood walk
jordaanwalk.tip: Wander the side streets and courtyards (hofjes) between Prinsengracht and Elandsgracht.

foodhallen.name: Foodhallen
foodhallen.tip: An indoor food market with many small stalls. Good for groups who want different food.

vondelpark.name: Vondelpark
vondelpark.tip: Rent a bike or just walk the loop. The terraces near the pond are busy on sunny days.

biketour.name: Guided bike tour
biketour.hours: Departures through the day · book ahead
biketour.tip: Cycling here is fast and rule-bound. A guided tour is safer than renting on your own first.

stays.why: Walk to Dam Square, the Anne Frank House and Centraal station. Busiest and priciest, but you save on transit.
Quiet canals, small galleries and cafés. Ten minutes on foot to the centre and the Anne Frank House.
Local feel, Albert Cuyp market and lots of food. Near the Museumplein for the big art museums.
Good value and a short tram ride to the centre. Popular with locals and repeat visitors.

food: Try Dutch snacks: bitterballen, raw herring from a stall, and stroopwafels fresh off the iron.
Albert Cuyp market in De Pijp is good for cheap eats; check opening hours on the day.
Indonesian rijsttafel is a Dutch classic; book ahead for dinner.
Cheap lunch: broodjes (sandwiches) and soup in cafés, roughly EUR 8–15.
Tap water is safe to drink. Carry a bottle and refill it.
more_time: Swap a city day for Haarlem: a short train ride, with a pretty centre and the Frans Hals museum. Check times and fares on the day.
Take the free ferry behind Centraal station to Amsterdam Noord for a different, quieter side of the city.
Rent a bike for a half day and ride the canals and the Vondelpark. Follow local rules and park only in marked spots.
